title: How to source programmers/software developers on Stackoverflow for free
description: In this video We are going to tell you how you how you can source software developers on StackOverflow for free. In this video, we will explore three methods of Sourcing  1. Tag based search 2. X-ray query on Google 3. Using data.stackexchange.com  I hope you will find your potential hire on Stackoverflow with the help of this video.  Sample X-ray query - (Javascript AND Angular) (Bangalore OR Pune) site:stackoverflow.com/users “1000.. reputation”  Link to use Plugin - https://recruitin.net/stackoverflow.php  Link to use Query on data.stackexhange.com - http://data.stackexchange.com/stackoverflow/query/597258/search-developers-on-location-and-skills  If you find this video useful please like and share OR if you have any query please comment down below.  Team QuodeIt https://www.quodeit.com

asr.full_text: For any company, the team is very critical. For a tech company, finding the right programmer with right skills and attitude is very important. One of the best ways to find programmers is Stack Overflow. What is Stack Overflow? Stack Overflow is one of the best places to find software engineers. Where over 5 million programmers from all over the world ask and answer queries related to programming. And they come here every day, not once every 18 months, like LinkedIn. So their Stack Overflow activity is going to be a better reflection of what they do, professionally. Thank their sparse LinkedIn profile. And the best thing about it all? Other Stack Overflow users rate every question and answer,. All of a given engineer's activity on Stack Overflow,. Which is then compiled into easily accessible profiles,. Along with links to professional blogs, Twitter, and anything else that you can imagine. The better question is, why aren't you sourcing on Stack Overflow? There are three ways to source programmers on Stack Overflow. First, tag-based search. Second, x-ray search on Google. And third, using data.stackoverflow.com. Tag based searches is the easiest and quickest to get the results. So we'll start with finding developers on the basis of tags. On the homepage of Stack Overflow, if you click on the tags option, it takes you to. The list of all the tags available. Tag is nothing but skills of a programmer. Although tags is very limited and you can't search based on location and many other things,. Tag based search can be very useful if you have the knowledge about what is the code. Technology you are looking for. If I am looking for a Python developer, here in the tags text box I will enter Python. Can see the website shows me all the available Python skills. If I click on. The Python tag it will take us to this page which contains all the questions. And answers for the Python tag. I know you're wondering where can you find. Developers. No worries just click on the top users over here. This shows us the top python skilled users based on their reputation in the last 30 days. And their reputation overall. Now what is reputation? Reputation is a rough measurement of how much the community trusts you. It is earned by convincing your peers that you know what you are talking about. Use of the site, including asking questions, answering, and suggesting edits, does not. Require any reputation at all. But the more reputation you earn, more the privileges you. Have. The primary way to gain reputation is by posting good questions and useful answers. Posts on these posts cause you to gain reputation. Please note that posts or posts marked Community Wiki do not generate any reputation. Now moving on to the second way of searching developers on Stack Overflow, which is X-Ray. Search on Google. With X-Ray Search, you can find people on the basis of skills plus location, so it would. Be more useful than the simple boolean search. You can also add reputation as one of the filters in your X-ray search. Say I have to hire a JavaScript developer who also should know Angular and she or he. Must be from Bangalore or Pune and also should have a reputation of thousand and more. This is how my X-ray query will look like. You see with one query, I get 20 results. Cool, isn't it? Let's look at this Arun P. Jony's profile in Stack Overflow. So this is his profile, Arun P. Jony. He has filled in quite a lot of details. A lot of people don't do this. There might be a chance that you won't be seeing. Much of information other people with stack overflow data you will be able to. See the following items reputation you see over here this is our own reputation. Stack overflow reputation is very hard to earn you get reputation when people. Upload the questions or answers you asked or given answer to reputation is a. Rough measure of how much the community trusts you your communication skills. The quality and relevance of your questions and answers. Moving on to badges. Besides gaining reputation with your questions and answers,. You receive badges as well for being especially. Helpful in specific topics. This guy has 39 gold, 313 silver, and 366 bronze badges. These badges are very hard to earn. And can speak a lot about a developer's knowledge. About the topic. Moving on to overall rank. Stack Overflow compares every profile. And shows you the rank. It shows rank in terms of overall percentage. The lesser the percentage, the greater the overall rank. Last scene. Last scene will tell you when was the last time. A developer visited the website. Or did any activity connected to this website. There are other profile data. Other profile details such as those of LinkedIn and GitHub would be very helpful to recruiters. As they don't have to search for particular candidate separately on those sites. The next segment is top tags. Top tags is the summation of the developer's activity in the Stack Overflow. These tags appear on the profile when a developer writes an answer or asks a question on Stack. Overflow for the particular tag. In Arun's case, his top tags are jQuery, JavaScript and CSS. Always check for a post percentage. It shows if the developer is asking more or writing more. If the developer is asking more, then he or she might be learning the particular topic. Higher post percentage can show the knowledge of the developer about this particular skill. The next topic is community. Stackoverflow.com is the question and answer site for programming discussions. On the similar ground, Stackoverflow Inc. created stackexchange.com, which has over. 60 question and answer forums in accordance with the top discussion. There are also plugins which build the X-ray searches depending upon the data you want. You will find one such plugin in the link in the description below. Moving on to the next. Source sync candidate with data.exchange.com. Stack Overflow Data Explorer is an open source tool for running arbitrary queries against. Public data from the Stack Exchange network. In simple terms, you can query whatever data. You want from the Stack Overflow network. Isn't that great? But here comes the tricky part. To be able to fetch the data from the Stack Overflow, you need to write a query. As we all. Know that it is a very difficult thing to do. Don't worry, I have already written a query which. Will be useful for you. You will find the link to the query in the description below. I have already pre-run the query here. In the query I've mentioned the location to be Pune,. Skill one and skill two to be Python and Django respectively and I've set the reputation to. Thousand. Upon running the query I get this table below. You see all the developer profiles are put. Into this table. I can also arrange these links as I require. Say for example if I require a. Developer who should not have much of Django score but should have a good knowledge that is a good. Score in Python I should set Python in descending order and you know what you can also pull this out. Into a CSV over here. So Stack Overflow is an awesome community of over 5 million developers. And a great place to source some kick-ass developers. It is very hard to predict the. Candidate's technical skills and knowledge just by looking at his LinkedIn profile. So don't worry,. Stack Overflow badges and reputation is the best way to know this. These things are very hard to. Earn and can speak a lot about a candidate's profile on this topic. To build a great Stack. Overflow profile, a person has to put his or her time to write good answers. There are many good. Developers present on Stack Overflow but are not active. There are also many great developers out. There who are not even on Stack Overflow. However, Stack Overflow is the community of over 5 million. Developers. Being able to source them on the basis of reputation and badges is very helpful. So guys, I'm Prasad from Coded. Coded is a Pune-based startup trying to save recruiters' time. Spent on initial filtering of programmers. If you found this video useful, do like and share. If you have any queries, do put them in the comment below. Peace!
